title: Measurement of mitochondrial respiratory chain enzymatic activities in Drosophila melanogaster samples
author: Brischigliaro, Frigo, et al.

steps.title: Collect Drosophila samples
steps.instruction: Gather the required number of flies or larvae for each biological replicate, keeping samples on ice. Timing: 0.5–2 h.

substeps.instruction: Adult flies: collect 80–100 flies per replicate.
Third‑instar larvae: collect 80–100 larvae per replicate. Add tap water with 20 % sugar to vials, let larvae detach, collect floating larvae, wash with PBS using a strainer.

Adult thoraces: dissect 120–150 thoraces per replicate. Anesthetize flies with CO₂, rinse quickly in 70 % ethanol, dissect heads, abdomen, wings and legs in ice‑cold PBS with tweezers and precision scissors.
Adjust numbers according to size; typically 80–100 larvae or 120–150 thoraces yield ~200–400 µg mitochondrial protein. Approximately 20–30 mg tissue is needed per preparation.

steps.title: Prepare isolation buffers
steps.instruction: Make all buffers fresh and store as indicated, keeping them ice‑cold before use.

substeps.instruction: MS (mannitol‑sucrose) buffer (200 mL total, store 4 °C, 1 week): 225 mM mannitol, 75 mM sucrose, 10 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.4, 1 mM EGTA, ddH₂O to volume.
MS + 1 % BSA: dissolve 1.5 g fatty‑acid‑free BSA in 150 mL of the MS buffer, store 4 °C, 1 week.
Tris‑HCl 10 mM pH 7.4 (store 4 °C, 1 month): dissolve 61 mg Tris base in 15 mL distilled H₂O, adjust pH to 7.4, bring volume to 50 mL with distilled H₂O.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue in buffer
steps.instruction: Homogenize each sample in ice‑cold MS + 1 % BSA buffer while keeping everything on ice.

substeps.instruction: Add 2–3 mL MS + BSA to the tissue.

Homogenize with 15–20 strokes at 1,000 rpm using a motor‑driven Teflon‑glass Elvehjem potter on ice. If a motor‑driven potter is unavailable, use a Dounce glass potter: loose‑fitting pestle for adults and third‑instar larvae, tight‑fitting pestle for thoraces and small larvae.
Maintain samples on ice throughout to prevent protein degradation.

steps.title: Transfer and rinse homogenate
steps.instruction: Collect the homogenate and rinse the potter to recover all material.

substeps.instruction: Transfer homogenate to a clean 30 mL centrifuge tube.
Rinse the potter with 7 mL MS + BSA and add the rinse to the same tube.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant (liquid phase) and discard the pellet containing unbroken cells and nuclei.

steps.title: Filter supernatant
steps.instruction: Remove large debris such as legs, wings and cuticle fragments.

substeps.instruction: Pass the supernatant through a 100 µm strainer into a new tube.

steps.title: First mitochondrial spin
steps.instruction: Pellet mitochondria from the filtered homogenate.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
A white lipid layer may adhere to the tube walls; remove it before proceeding.

steps.title: Wash mitochondria (first)
steps.instruction: Resuspend and re‑spin to clean the mitochondrial pellet.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL MS + 1 % BSA.
Repeat the 6,000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C spin (same as step 7).

steps.title: Wash mitochondria (second)
steps.instruction: Remove BSA from the mitochondrial preparation.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL MS buffer without BSA.
Centrifuge at 7,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend final pellet
steps.instruction: Prepare the mitochondrial suspension for downstream assays.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 300–400 µL MS buffer without BSA.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure mitochondrial protein concentration using any standard assay.

substeps.instruction: Perform Bradford, Lowry, or BCA assay in triplicate, setting up a standard curve for consistency and reliability.

steps.title: Store mitochondrial preparation
steps.instruction: Preserve the isolated mitochondria for later use.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot the suspension to avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.
Store at –80 °C for up to 3 months. Avoid multiple freeze‑thaw cycles, which can reduce enzyme activities.

description: This protocol describes step-by-step how to measure the enzymatic activity of the MRC complexes in isolated mitochondria obtained from different Drosophila melanogaster tissues. Firstly, mitochondria are separated from homogenized tissues through differential centrifugation using a sucrose-based buffer. Then, mitochondria membranes are disrupted to allow the substrates to access the MRC complexes. Enzymatic activities of individual MRC complexes are measured using specific kinetic assays and UV-VIS spectrophotometry. The MRC activities measured in this way are often normalized to the activity of the citrate synthase, a mitochondrial matrix enzyme of the Krebs cycle that is considered as a good marker of mitochondrial volume. This detailed protocol builds on previously described methods for the isolation of mitochondria from D. melanogaster tissues (Brischigliaro et al., 2019; Brischigliaro et al., 2021) and on the procedures for measuring MRC enzymatic activities in human samples (Bugiani et al., 2004; Kirby et al., 2007; Spinazzi et al., 2012; Trounce et al., 1996). However, extensive optimization was carried out by the authors in order to provide a detailed and step-by-step procedure easy to follow also for newcomers. Essential material you must have/prepare:1.Biological samples: adult files or larvae.2.Refer to key resources table and materials and equipment to prepare reagents and buffers.
